verdict.summary: PSIX makes engines and packaged power systems, including the gensets data centers buy for backup and prime power, and is majority-owned by China's Weichai. The stock collapsed 74% from its February high to $25.28 on July 29, then reclaimed 63% in seven sessions. The last leg was a +21% gap on Friday, off Thursday evening's Q2 print: revenue $152.5M against a $134M estimate, gross margin up 420bps sequentially to 27.1%, $30.8M of debt paid down in one quarter. Set against that: a 7.3M-share float with 23.9% of it sold short, and a chart still below its 200-day average. This is a momentum-and-squeeze trade with defined risk, not a quality compounder. Our five-persona value board votes 4/5 bearish at this price.
whyBuy: Q2 revenue of $152.5M beat the $134M estimate by 14% and grew 18.6% over Q1, the sequential inflection the bulls were waiting for after two soft quarters.
Gross margin of 27.1% (up ~420bps from Q1) plus $30.8M of debt reduction in the quarter: operational repair showing up in the numbers, not just the narrative.
Squeeze mechanics: 1.76M shares short (FINRA, July 15 settlement) on a 7.3M float, i.e. 23.9%, with 3.9 days to cover, and call OI stacked 3.5:1 over puts into August 21 expiry.

Management guides second-half sales roughly in line with H2 2025 as larger Power Systems orders enter production, materially stronger than the H1 run-rate, with data center demand called out as solid.
EV/EBITDA at 10.2x and trailing earnings around $3.00/share put the P/E near 13x: not deep value after the gap, but low enough that a durable margin repair re-rates it.
whyAvoid: The growth optics are still negative: revenue fell 21% year-over-year and EPS of $0.73 compares with $2.24 a year ago. The two 2026 quarters both missed a consensus that is only one or two analysts wide.
Price sits 26.2% above its own 20-day average after two unfilled gaps. A fill of Friday's gap is roughly -20% to $33 without invalidating anything fundamental.
Governance churn: third CEO since May (Xykis out, CFO Li interim, Richard Hu effective August 17), inside a company ~63% insider-held with Weichai in control. The tiny float cuts both ways.

Our deterministic value/quality board votes 4/5 bearish: operating margin 8.9%, gross margin 24.3% TTM, debt-to-equity 0.91, price 41% above its Graham number. Multi-method intrinsic valuation returned no verdict; the cash-flow inputs it requires are not published on our data surface, so we won't pretend to a fair value.

business.overview: Power Solutions International (Wood Dale, Illinois, ~1,000 employees) designs and manufactures engines and integrated power systems: emission-certified engines, custom-engineered generator sets for standby and prime power, enclosures and electrification components. Its power systems serve data centers, oil & gas, microgrids, demand response and rental fleets; industrial products power forklifts and off-road equipment; a transportation line serves trucks and specialty vehicles. The company is majority-owned by Weichai America (insiders hold 63.2% overall), which leaves a public float of roughly 7.3M shares out of 23.1M outstanding. The 2026 story is a mix shift: larger Power Systems orders (data center gensets prominent among them) moving into production while the legacy industrial and transportation lines digest a soft first half.
business.theme: Data center backup and prime power demand, executed by a controlled small-cap with a locked-up float.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Positively verified over a 5-year EDGAR sweep (2020-2026, ~100 filings): no S-3 shelf, no 424B prospectus, no 8-K item 3.02 (unregistered equity sales). The 8-K items 1.01/2.03 on file are credit-facility agreements, not equity issuance. The 2013-era warrants ($13.00/$13.20 strikes) were exercised or expired by 2016. Share count has been stable at ~23M.

technicals.setupNote: The structure is a broken downtrend attempting a V: 52-week high $121.78 (August 2025), February high near $97, then a five-month slide to $25.28 on July 29. The reversal came in two gaps, +4.5% on August 4 and +13.1% on Friday, neither filled. Price at $41 sits 26.2% above the 20-day EMA ($32.58), above the 50-day ($37.33), and well below the 200-day ($53.82). Friday's intraday range ran $38.28-$42.03, with the June range high at $43.23 the last shelf before the air pocket the May collapse left behind: there is little traded volume between $43 and the mid-$50s. ATR is ~$3 and options imply ±10% over two weeks. Size for that, not for a normal industrial.

risks.riskSummary: The risk is not dilution or solvency; both check out clean. It is buying a 2-beta, 100%-IV controlled company 26% above its 20-day average, the day after a print the (very thin) consensus scored as an EPS miss. A 10-15 session hold also crosses the mid-August macro calendar (CPI, Jackson Hole): at beta 2.1, one risk-off tape can hit the stop with zero PSIX news.

tradeIdea.thesis: Q2 showed real operational repair (a 14% revenue beat, 420bps of sequential gross-margin gain, $30.8M of debt retired) into a 7.3M-share float carrying 23.9% short interest positioned during the slide to $25. Above $43.23 there is almost no traded supply until the mid-$50s. The consensus headline read 'EPS miss'; Friday's tape read the revenue line and gapped 21%. We side with the tape, tactically, at half size.

Richard Hu takes over as CEO August 17, the first outside operator hire (ex-BorgWarner) after months of interim leadership
Short covering: 1.76M shares short vs ~447K average daily volume, 3.9 days to cover at normal tape
Q3 print (November 5) is the checkpoint for the guided H2 Power Systems ramp
invalidation: Daily close below $34.86 (the August 4 close): Friday's gap is filling and the reversal failed. Exit, no averaging down
Still below $38 at the August 21 close: the squeeze didn't take and the position has no edge left. Close it even without the stop
